But even just two weeks of this has made improvements.

What a lot of people fail to recognize (including myself) is that you need at least some semblance of a cardio base. Especially in some basic exercise science courses, you get taught this idea that the body's energy systems are kind of discrete entities. If you are working at maximal effort for under 10 seconds, it's all alactic. If you are working from 20 seconds to 2 minutes, it's lactic. More than that and its aerobic.

The reality is all systems are working all the time. What I've discovered from looking at data on "repeat sprint" athletes (think football, or fighting, or tennis even), is that the aerobic system is working from the get go, and it is the main factor that replenishes the substrate of the alactic and lactic systems. Meaning in activities where you have repeated (but intermittent) maximal efforts, those anaerobic systems are replenished more efficiently by a strong aerobic base. In other words, weight training is benefited by having an aerobic base.

No more excuses not to at least have some cardio. I don't ever intend to run a marathon, but I'd like to have the capacity to run 20-30 minutes without thinking about it, and then just maintain that for as long as possible. Also throw in some sprinting once or twice weekly.
